facts.fact_text: A demonstration was planned to be held on 20 October 2012 in Baku.
A demonstration was planned to be held on 17 November 2012 in Baku.
Each applicant attended one of the two demonstrations held on 20 October 2012 or 17 November 2012 in Baku (as specified in the Appendix).
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
Shortly after the demonstrations had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
All applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations.
All applicants were taken to various police stations following their arrest.
The Baku City Executive Authority refused to authorise the demonstration of 20 October 2012 at the place indicated by the organisers.

The Baku City Executive Authority proposed an alternative location for the demonstration of 20 October 2012 on the outskirts of Baku, specifically the yard of a driving school situated in the 20th habitable area of the Sabail District.
The Baku City Executive Authority refused to authorise the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
The Baku City Executive Authority noted in general terms that the assembly planned for 17 November 2012 would not be in accordance with the Law on Freedom of Assembly.
The Baku City Executive Authority noted that the square where the organisers proposed to hold the assembly planned for 17 November 2012 was a designated public leisure area.
The Baku City Executive Authority noted that the assembly planned for 17 November 2012 would be impractical.

The Baku City Executive Authority noted that the square where the organisers proposed to hold the assembly planned for 17 November 2012 was a designated public leisure area.
The Baku City Executive Authority noted that the assembly planned for 17 November 2012 would be impractical.
Shortly after the demonstrations had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
All applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations.
All applicants were taken to various police stations following their arrest.
On the day of each applicant's arrest, administrative offence reports (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) were issued on the applicants.

The administrative offence reports stated that by deliberately failing to comply with a lawful order of the police, the applicants had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The courts sentenced the applicants to a period of administrative detention varying from five to thirteen days (as specified in the Appendix).
The applicant in application no. 8468/13 was additionally convicted under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after their arrest.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer while they were in police custody.
Each applicant was brought before a first-instance court on the day of their arrest.
According to most of the applicants, the hearing before the court in each case was very brief.
Members of the public were not allowed inside the courtroom during the respective hearings.
According to all applicants, they were not given an opportunity to appoint lawyers of their own choosing at the first-instance court hearings.
State-funded lawyers were invited to represent most of the applicants at the first-instance court hearings.
The applicants in application nos. 8204/13, 31201/13 and 51930/13 were not represented by a lawyer at the first-instance court hearings.

According to the transcripts of the respective court hearings, the applicants in application nos. 8204/13 and 51930/13 refused the assistance of a State-funded lawyer and decided to defend themselves in person.
The applicants stated in the respective first-instance courts that they were not guilty of failing to comply with a lawful order of the police.
According to the transcripts of the hearings, in their oral submissions the State-funded lawyers stated in general terms that the applicants were not guilty.
According to the transcripts of the hearings, in their oral submissions the State-funded lawyers briefly asked the respective courts to adopt a fair decision.
